_comment: Reviewed holes in the cross-language artifact-role parity gate
(datrix/scripts/test/artifact-role-parity-gate.ps1). Each entry names one
(example, domain, language) coordinate where that language's blessed baseline
has zero files matching the domain's structural_pattern, even though >= 1
other blessed language for the SAME example has one. This is a genuine,
reviewed gap -- never a suppression of an unexplained finding.
Every entry below was investigated by reading the actual blessed manifest
paths and the declared structural_pattern before being recorded. Two
further categories of apparent divergence turned out to be fixable in the
gate's OWN classifier rather than needing an exemption at all (see
_pattern_specificity's most-specific-match tie-break and
_PACKAGE_MARKER_BASENAMES in artifact_role_parity.py) -- a shallower
sibling domain's glob no longer steals credit from a deeper, more
specific one, and a bare package-init marker (e.g. __init__.py) is never
credited to any domain. What remains below are the genuine gaps:
(1) dotnet's helper/Support/*.cs output is emitted only when the DSL
invokes a gating builtin category or an extension that declares its
own Support helper; python/typescript/java instead always emit
baseline helper-utility scaffolding regardless of DSL content.
expected_count is a pinned, reviewed value: change it only in the same
change that adds or removes an entry.

Verified against the DSL source (loan-service.dtrx/member-service.dtrx/common.dtrx): no Auth./Json./Validator./Request. builtin calls (the `request.bookId`/`request.memberId` occurrences are references to an inter-service call's own response variable named `request`, not `Request.*` builtin property-access calls), no Log.withContext/setLevel, no Geo/GeoShape/Crypto.sign, no extension usage, no Crypto.* call at all. python's blessed manifest always emits _datrix_helpers.py regardless of DSL content -- the same genuine per-language boilerplate-emission design difference the other entries in this file record, not a missing capability.

dotnet emits Support/*.cs only when the DSL invokes a gating builtin category (Auth/JSON/Validator/Request/Log) or an extension that declares its own Support helper (e.g. the geo extension, where dotnet's Support/GeoHelpers.cs is present and this domain is not exempted for that example). This example invokes none of those, so dotnet's blessed baseline holds zero Support files. python/typescript/java instead always emit baseline helper-utility scaffolding (_datrix_helpers.py, _archiveHelpers.ts, MapSupport.java) regardless of DSL content. A genuine per-language boilerplate-emission design difference, not a missing capability.

Python's declared nosql_test structural_pattern (*/tests/unit/docdb/test_*.py) hardcodes the literal nosql-block directory name 'docdb' from the original nosql-blocks example instead of a block-name wildcard. This example's nosql block is named 'analytics', so python's real, present output (tests/unit/analytics/test_reading_history.py -- verified in the freshly generated tree) does not match the declared literal. A structural_pattern precision gap in the classifier's declared glob, not a missing capability: python does generate nosql_test-domain output for this example. Widening the pattern to a bare block wildcard was rejected because it would tie in specificity with cache_test's own pattern at the same path depth and falsely credit nosql_test for a redis cache-test file; tracked as a follow-up task in the owning package's task queue since the correct fix needs a per-domain multi-pattern or negative-match capability the current DomainDeclaration shape does not have.
